summary: This regulation explains how a listed company must share its annual report, director details, and auditor information with shareholders. It also covers how disclosures must be sent to stock exchanges. The rules help shareholders stay informed about company leadership and money matters.
points: Send soft copies of the full annual report to shareholders who registered their email addresses.
Send a letter with the web-link for the annual report to shareholders who have not registered their email.
Send a hard copy of the annual report to any shareholder who asks for it.
Provide specific background and experience details to shareholders when appointing or re-appointing a director.
Send disclosures to stock exchanges in XBRL format and ensure they can be easily searched by users.
Include proposed auditor fees, appointment terms, and recommendation reasons in the meeting notice when appointing an auditor.
example: Aarav Steel Limited wanted to hold its annual general meeting and needed to share important updates with its investors. For shareholders like Rohan who registered their email, the company sent a soft copy of the full annual report. For Priya, who had not shared her email, the company mailed a letter with the exact web-link to the report. Meanwhile, investor Kabir asked for a physical copy, so Aarav Steel Limited mailed him a hard copy. When the company proposed a new director, it shared the director's brief resume, skills, and past directorships with all shareholders so they could make an informed choice.

terms.meaning: A yearly document showing a company's financial health and business activities.
An organization that holds shares and securities safely in electronic form.
A computer-readable file format used for business and financial data reporting.
An official independent accountant appointed to check the company financial accounts.

watch: Do not forget that hard copies of the annual report are only sent if a shareholder specifically requests one.
